channel.title: Mathematical Physics Lab — Frontier Radar — 数論・ラングランズ
channel.description: 数学・数学のためのAI・基礎物理学の最先端を、arXiv の全数学分野と高エネルギー物理の新着、キーワード別に数年分さかのぼった arXiv 検索、最上位の学術誌、一流研究者のブログ、主要な賞の報道からまるごと集め、重要度で順位づけする検索型RSSリーダー。

item.title: On Hilbert's tenth problem for number fields
item.description: Given a quadratic number field $K$ we show that the $abc$ conjecture over $K$ implies that $\mathbb{Z}$ is Diophantine in $K$ and, hence, a negative answer to Hilbert's tenth problem over $K$. More generally, the same conclusions hold for an arbitrary number field $K$ provided that the $abc$ conjecture holds over $K$ and that there is an elliptic curve over $\mathbb{Q}$ whose rank is positive and does not increase over $K$. — Hector Pasten, Xavier Vidaux — arXiv math.CO / LO / cs.DM / cs.CC / cs.DS / arXiv math.NT / AG / RT / RA / AC / arXiv: elliptic

item.title: On metric multiplicative Diophantine approximation
item.description: Gallagher's theorem (1962) gives a Khintchine-type dichotomy for the Lebesgue measure of the set of multiplicatively $\psi$-approximable points in $\mathbb{R}^n$, $n \geq 2$, for monotonic functions $\psi$. We establish this dichotomy for arbitrary functions $\psi$, proving a conjecture of Beresnevich, Haynes, and Velani (2013). — Manuel Hauke-Treuer, Felipe A. Ramirez — arXiv math.NT / AG / RT / RA / AC

item.title: Landau's problems through ratios of $L$-functions
item.description: Very recently, Lee announced a proof of the Twin Prime Conjecture assuming the Ratios Conjecture for the Riemann zeta function. We obtain conditional asymptotic formulas with power-saving errors for each of Landau's four prime problems. In the function field setting, using Sawin's estimates for factorization functions in squarefree progressions and a discriminant cohomology argument, we obtain unconditional Goldbach and prime-pair asymptotics over sufficiently large fixed odd fields, including prime fields… — Haozhe Gou, Victor Y. Wang, Max Wenqiang Xu — arXiv: primes / arXiv: riemann

item.title: Why should $\mathbbZ$ be Diophantine in $\mathbbQ$?
item.description: We give a Diophantine definition of the integers in the rational numbers conditional on the $abc$ conjecture, Dickson's conjecture, and finiteness of $2$-primary parts of Shafarevich--Tate groups. We also discuss some consequences of the existence of a Diophantine definition of the integers in the rational numbers. The goal of this work is to serve as an entry point to recent developments around Hilbert's tenth problem for the rational numbers. — Alexander Kozachinskiy, Hector Pasten, Xavier Vidaux — arXiv: elliptic

item.title: A Diophantine definition of $\mathbbZ$ in $\mathbbQ$
item.description: We prove that the integers form a Diophantine subset of the rational numbers. More precisely, there exist an integer $n\ge1$ and a polynomial $P\in\mathbb{Z}[T,W_1,\dots,W_n]$ of total degree at most four such that $q\in\mathbb{Q}$ is an integer if and only if $P(q,\mathbf w)=0$ for some $\mathbf w\in\mathbb{Q}^n$. Consequently, any recursively enumerable subset of $\mathbb{Q}^r$ is Diophantine, and Mazur's conjecture on the topology of rational points fails. The proof is inspired by OpenAI's work on Hilbert's… — Ashay Burungale — arXiv: elliptic / arXiv: modularity

item.title: Proof of the Quasi Riemann Hypothesis using $\mathbb Q[i]$
item.description: Using quartic Gauss sums in place of the cubic Gauss sums in OpenAI's original proof, we prove that the Dedekind $ζ$-function $ζ_{\mathbb Q(i)}(s)$ of $\mathbb Q(i)$ has no zeros in the half-plane $\Re s>599/600$, thereby obtaining the same zero-free half-plane for the Riemann $ζ$-function.We obtain the upper bound for the smoothed sum by applying Poisson summation twice and using the functional equation of the quartic Kubota series of angular weight $1$.In the Mellin representation, a zero-density bound for the… — XinHang Ji — arXiv: riemann

item.title: On elliptic curves with prescribed analytic rank at least $2$
item.description: Zywina recently showed that infinitely many elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}$ have rank $2$, settling a long-standing open question. We explore the analytic version of this problem, showing that every elliptic curve over $\mathbb{Q}$ has infinitely many quadratic twists with analytic rank either $2$ or $4$, subject to GRH. We also obtain, under the same assumption, infinitely many congruent number curves with odd analytic rank between $3$ and $17$. — Francesco Naccarato — arXiv: elliptic

item.title: Local-global compatibility with $p$-adic Langlands program for completed (co)homology of $\mathrmGL_2$ over CM fields
item.description: For each place $v \mid p$ such that $F_v \simeq \mathbf{Q}_p$, we establish a compatibility with $p$-adic Langlands program for completed homology with integral coefficients for $\mathrm{GL}_2$ over CM fields $F$ with $[F:\mathbf{Q}]>2$, after localization with respect to a non-Eisenstein decomposed generic maximal ideal of a Hecke algebra. — Jelena Ivancic — arXiv math.NT / AG / RT / RA / AC / arXiv: langlands

item.title: On the self-extensions of the mod $p$ Jacquet-Langlands correspondence over $\mathbbQ_p$
item.description: Let $p\ge5$ and $D$ be the unique nonsplit quaternion algebra over $\mathbb{Q}_p$. We compute, in the category of smooth representations with a fixed central character, the self-extension groups of the $D^{\times}$-representations occurring in the mod $p$ Jacquet-Langlands correspondence in the generic case. The main ingredient is a new weighted filtration on the relevant ring and module. The associated graded module preserves the first nontrivial extension relation, which is not detected by the… — Chenhao Tang — arXiv math.NT / AG / RT / RA / AC / arXiv: langlands

item.title: Spectral action in Betti metaplectic Langlands
item.description: We construct the spectral action in the context of Betti metaplectic Langlands theory. More precisely, we prove that the category of twisted sheaves on $\text{Bun}_G$ with nilpotent singular support admits a canonical action by the symmetric monoidal category of quasicoherent sheaves on the moduli of twisted $H$-local systems, where $H$ is the metaplectic dual group. This confirms the Betti version of the conjecture of Gaitsgory--Lysenko, originally formulated in the de Rham setting under the name ``metaplectic… — JiWoong Park — arXiv: langlands

item.title: Invariant distributions and common denominators in the Bernstein center
item.description: Let $G$ be a connected reductive group over a non-Archimedean local field. We conjecture that every invariant distribution whose support is compact modulo conjugation belongs to the rational Bernstein center. We also make an explicit conjecture about the ideal of possible denominators (the description is using a version of the local Langlands correspondence and involves working with endoscopic subgroups of $G$). We prove this for products of general linear groups; in this case the above idea is much more explicit… — Alexander Braverman, David Kazhdan — arXiv: langlands

item.title: Pair Correlation Conjecture for the Zeros of Artin $L$-functions I: Simple and Critical Zeros
item.description: In 1973, Montgomery posed the pair correlation conjecture (PCC) for the zeros of the Riemann zeta function. Motivated by PCC, Montgomery conjectured that the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function are almost surely simple, and proved that at least $2/3$ are simple assuming the Riemann hypothesis (RH). In 1978, Mueller and Gallagher were able to prove asymptotically $100\%$ are simple assuming PCC and RH. Recently, Goldston et al. noticed that the assumption of RH can be removed in Mueller and Gallagher's… — Vincent Nguyen — arXiv: riemann

item.title: On p-adic asymptotic formulas for slope factors of L-functions of toric exponential sums
item.description: Adolphson and Sperber expressed the unique unit root of the $L$-function of a toric exponential sum in terms of $A$-hypergeometric functions, whereas reciprocal zeros and poles of positive slope remain much less understood.We study complete rational factors of arbitrary prescribed slope in families satisfying a chain-level ordinary condition. Our main tool is a new contraction map arising from a twisted block LU factorization of the Frobenius matrix of a nuclear $\sigma$-module. Its fixed point produces an upper… — Chunlin Wang — arXiv math.NT / AG / RT / RA / AC / arXiv: riemann

item.title: $\mathbb Z$ is diophantine over $\mathbb Q$ with 26 unknowns
item.description: Recently, OpenAI proved that Hilbert's Tenth Problem over the field $\mathbb Q$ of rational numbers has a negative solution. Motivated by this work, G. Conant et al. showed that $\mathbb Z$ is diophantine over $\mathbb Q$, i.e., there is an integer-coefficient polynomial $F(x,y_1,\ldots,y_n)$ such that for any $x\in\mathbb Q$ we have $$ x\in\mathbb Z\quad\iff \exists\,y_1,\ldots,y_{n}\in\mathbb Q\ [F(x,y_1,\ldots,y_{n})=0].$$ They constructed such a polynomial $F$ with $°F=4$ and $n=221$.In this paper, we prove… — Zhi-Wei Sun — arXiv: elliptic

item.title: When do all iterates of $x^2 + a$ have maximal Galois group?
item.description: We provide an (in our opinion) simpler proof of the main results of [Stoll1992,Li2020,Li2021] on the question for which integers $a$ the Galois groups of all iterates of $x^2 + a$ are maximal (equivalently, the associated arboreal Galois representation is surjective). At the same time, we extend the results to rational parameters $a$. The main result states that for a subset of rational numbers of relative density $1/2$ in the complement of a certain open interval, the maximality of the Galois group of the second… — Michael Stoll — arXiv: lean / arXiv: modularity

item.title: Gram's law for moving targets of the Riemann zeta-function
item.description: We study the solutions of $ζ(s)=f(s)$ for targets $f$ that grow with $|s|$, and Gram's law for them: the statement that each shifted Gram interval contains exactly one solution. The deviation from Gram's law is an integer phase-slip counter, equal up to rounding to $-\frac{1}{2}S(t;x_c)$, where $S(t;x)=π^{-1}\argζ(x+it)$ and $x_c\approx 1/2+\log|f(it)|/\log t$ is a balance abscissa determined by the target. If $|f|\asymp t^κ$ with $κ>κ_1=0.5339\ldots$, where $\sum_p\arcsin(p^{-1/2-κ_1})=π$, and $\arg f$… — Ryan Goulden — arXiv: riemann

item.title: Complex Moments of the Derivative of the Riemann Zeta Function
item.description: We investigate the complex moments of the derivative of the Riemann zeta function through a random Euler product model. For each fixed $σ>1/2$ and every $s\in\mathbb{C}$ with $\operatorname{Re}(s)>0$, we show, under the Lindelöf hypothesis, that the $2s$-th moment of $|ζ'(σ+\mathrm{i}t)|$ over $t\in[1,T]$ converges, as $T\to\infty$, to the corresponding moment of the derivative of the random Euler product. We then establish, unconditionally, an asymptotic formula for the latter moment as $σ\downarrow 1/2$… — Joseph Najnudel, Fei Wei — arXiv: riemann

item.title: Polar states in AdS$_3$ holography
item.description: Modularity determines the elliptic genus of $\textrm{Sym}^N(\mathrm{K3})$ at finite $N$ from the indexed degeneracies of polar states, which are states that lie below the black hole threshold in AdS$_3$/CFT$_2$. We propose that each polar degeneracy is reproduced exactly by one-loop contributions from a finite set of asymmetric $(\mathrm{AdS}_3 \times \mathrm{S}^3)/\mathbb{Z}_K \times \mathrm{K3}$ backgrounds in type IIB string theory. We compute the classical charges of these backgrounds using supergravity and… — Ji Hoon Lee, Wei Li — arXiv: modularity

item.title: The Fourier kernel and invariant trace formula of $mGL(3)$
item.description: Trace formula is an important method to study the Langlands program. Arthur obtains the existence of stable trace formula for connected reductive group. In this paper, we will give the explicit invariant trace formula of GL(3). For general reductive groups, Arthur gave an inductive proof of the existence of the invariant trace formula and provided explicit examples for GL(2). For GL(3), we successively compute the invariant distributions, give all the Fourier kernels for the GL(2) cases, and finally obtain the… — Haoyang Wang, Xinghua Cui, Zhifeng Peng — arXiv: langlands

item.title: Two-Sided large oscillations of the argument of the Riemann zeta function and its iterates
item.description: Assuming the Riemann hypothesis, we establish lower bounds for large oscillations of the iterated argument functions \(S_n(t)\) of the Riemann zeta function. As a corollary, we prove that, for every fixed integer \(n \geq 0\), \[S_n(t)=Ω_{\pm}\Big(\frac{(\log t)^{1/2}(\log_3 t)^{1/2}}{(\log_2 t)^{n+1/2}} \Big).\] For even \(n\), this recovers two results of Chirre and Mahatab in 2021. For odd \(n\), our result strengthens theirs by establishing the missing direction of oscillation with the same order of magnitude. — Shengbo Zhao — arXiv: riemann

item.title: On p-adic modularity of abelian threefolds with imaginary multiplication and rational p-isogeny
item.description: We prove $p$-adic modularity of a certain class of abelian threefolds over $\mathbf{Q}$ (with imaginary multiplication and rational $p$-isogeny), including the Jacobians of some genus 3 curves known as Picard curves. More precisely, we study a deformation problem for residual 3-dimensional totally reducible Galois pseudorepresentations over an imaginary quadratic field which are ordinary at primes over $p$ and conjugate self-dual. We show that under certain conditions the universal pseudodeformation ring in any… — Tobias Berger, Krzysztof Klosin — arXiv: modularity

item.title: Quantum Langlands correspondence for Painlevé II
item.description: We construct an irregular KZ-BPZ correspondence for quantum Painlevé II from a rank-three Wakimoto-Whittaker module. The irregular KZ equation and the quantum isomonodromy equation form a joint affine system whose Drinfeld-Sokolov reduction yields scalar BPZ equations. We obtain matrix-integral solutions of this system for one fundamental insertion. An exact quantum Langlands duality exchanges the fundamental insertion with the zero of the dual Whittaker differential and allows affine solutions to be… — Sibasish Banerjee, Babak Haghighat, Jie Sun — arXiv: langlands

item.title: Motivic generating functions and $L$-derivatives of cohomological automorphic representations
item.description: Forty years ago, Gross and Zagier proved a remarkable formula computing the central derivative of the Rankin--Selberg $L$-function of a cusp form $f$ of weight $2$ and a character of the class group of an imaginary quadratic field, satisfying the so-called Heegner condition, and deduce that the nonvanishing of the central derivative implies the nonvanishing of the corresponding Mordell--Weil rank. This formula was later generalized in various contexts and degrees, for example, by S. Zhang for $f$ of higher even… — Yifeng Liu — arXiv: riemann

item.title: Conformal field theory from automorphic forms on a quantum group
item.description: We reformulate two-dimensional conformal field theory (2d CFT) in the language of noncommutative geometry. To this end, we introduce automorphic forms for the von Neumann algebraic quantum group $\mathrm{SL}^+_b(2,\mathbb{R})$. A quantum measure space is a von Neumann algebra equipped with a weight. We study such spaces carrying a weight-preserving action of $\mathrm{SL}^+_b(2,\mathbb{R})$. We argue that every unitary bosonic 2d CFT with central charge $c=1+6(b+b^{-1})^2>1$ is equivalent to a quantum measure… — Dalimil Mazac — arXiv: bootstrap

item.title: MegaOps: A Kernel Overlapping Framework with PyTorch-like Modularity and Megakernel Performance
item.description: Modern ML frameworks execute models using the kernel-per-operator paradigm, which runs each operator as a separate GPU kernel. This paradigm is modular, since developers can compose various kernel implementations and profile each kernel in isolation. However, this paradigm enforces dependencies at the granularity of entire kernels, which places a barrier between dependent kernels. These barriers cause streaming multiprocessors to idle, serialize computation and communication, and prevent a kernel from prefetching… — Jinkun Lin, Byungsoo Oh, Rachee Singh — arXiv: modularity

item.title: Zeros of Katz's p-adic Eisenstein series E2
item.description: For every prime $p\geq5$, the zeros of Katz's $p$-adic Eisenstein series $E_2$ on elliptic curves with good ordinary reduction have exactly $\lfloor p/12\rfloor+1$ distinct $j$-invariants. We prove that all these invariants lie in finite unramified extensions of $\mathbf{Q}_p$. Their reductions are given by a classical formula involving the supersingular polynomial, and each nonelliptic residue class contains a unique simple zero. For the Legendre family, hypergeometric congruences determine the polynomial of the… — Abdellah Sebbar, Khalil Besrour — arXiv: elliptic / arXiv: modularity

item.title: The distribution of small gaps between zeros of the Riemann zeta function
item.description: Let $0<γ_1\leq γ_2\leq \cdots$ be the ordinates of the non-trivial zeros $ρ_n$ of the Riemann zeta function in the upper half-plane, counted with multiplicity. Selberg proved unconditionally that there exists $λ_0<1$ such that a positive proportion of the zeros $ρ_n$ satisfy $γ_{n+1}-γ_n\leq 2πλ_0/\log γ_n$. Simonič, Trudgian and Turnage-Butterbaugh were the first to obtain an explicit value in Selberg's theorem, showing that $λ_0=1- 10^{-3\cdot 10^{13}}$ is admissible. This was considerably improved by Zhao who… — Youness Lamzouri — arXiv: riemann

item.title: Symplectic singularities in Relative Langlands duality for products of general linear groups
item.description: It was shown by Braverman-Finkelberg-Nakajima that the regular perverse sheaf on the affine Grassmannian of type A is isomorphic to the ring object associated to a Gelfand-Tsetlin quiver. We use this result to identify, for any finite dimensional representation $\mathbf{N}$ of a product of general linear groups, the relative Langlands dual $(T^*\mathbf{N})^\vee$ of $T^*\mathbf{N}$ with the Coulomb branch of a suitable representation. By a result of Bellamy, this implies that $(T^*\mathbf{N})^\vee$ has symplectic… — Bruno da Silveira Dias, Victor Ginzburg — arXiv: langlands

item.title: Elliptic units, derived Heegner classes and the p-adic Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer quotient of CM elliptic curves of rank two
item.description: Let $E\colon y^2=x^3-Dx$ have rank two and let $p\equiv1\pmod4$ be a prime of good reduction. We study the conjecture that the $p$-adic quotient $q_p$, the leading coefficient of the cyclotomic $p$-adic $L$-function divided by the Euler factor and the $p$-adic regulator, equals the complex quotient $q_\infty=L''(E,1)/(2Ω_E\mathrm{Reg}_\infty)$, and that the latter is rational. In rank one the analogous statement is a theorem of Perrin-Riou and Rubin, because a Heegner point computes both sides; in rank two there… — Miquel Calonge Fabregat — arXiv: elliptic / arXiv: riemann

item.title: A complete symmetric rank-two modularity classification, obtained through a sharp uniform degree bound
item.description: We classify modular Nahm sums with a rational symmetric positive-definite two-by-two matrix and rational shifts. Up to coordinate exchange, every modular datum belongs to three explicit rational-point families, is a product of two modular rank-one sums, or is one of thirty-four exceptional triples on twelve matrices. The list consists of Zagier's rank-two examples, the Vlasenko--Zwegers additions and split products; no further data occur. The proof first bounds the joint degree of the distinguished Nahm point by… — Cetin Hakimoglu-Brown — arXiv: modularity

item.title: Compatible Hamel Topologies, Real Valued Isomorphisms and Rational Scalar Continuity
item.description: We study Hamel character topologies on the real line in two parts. Part I treats the full real-orbit (TVG) and the rational-parameter (TVGQ) dual pairs. A divisibility-chain criterion decides compatibility on the rationals and on Q/Z. Compatible subsets of one chain have a compatible join, but two different chains need not: an explicit Chinese remainder construction gives two compatible topologies with an incompatible join. This answers the compact-union question negatively, disproves the Greatest Compatible TVG… — Irina Yaroshevskaya — arXiv: modularity

item.title: Nontrivial Zeros of the Riemann Zeta Function and Its Derivative
item.description: The nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function lie at the heart of analytic number theory. Through the explicit formulas, they govern the distribution of prime numbers: the closer all nontrivial zeros lie to the critical line $\Re(s)=\frac12$, the more uniformly the primes are distributed. The Riemann Hypothesis-asserting that all nontrivial zeros satisfy $\Re(s)=\frac12$-is equivalent to the optimal error bound $O(\sqrt{x}\log x)$ in the Prime Number Theorem. Beyond number theory, the zeros of $ζ(s)$ and its… — Chuancun Yin, Xianghua Zhao, Zuolu Hao, Zhongyang Sun — arXiv: riemann

item.title: Smooth approximations to character sums and zeta sums
item.description: We study smooth approximations to Dirichlet character sums and zeta sums. The uniform upper-bound consequence of the Granville--Soundararajan conjecture, when imposed on all nonprincipal characters including imprimitive ones, implies the Riemann hypothesis for every primitive nonprincipal Dirichlet \(L\)-function. The proof uses characters induced to moduli divisible by all small primes. In the other direction, assuming the Riemann hypothesis for \(L(s,χ)\), we establish the conjectured approximation uniformly… — Zikang Dong, Shengbo Zhao, Guang-Liang Zhou — arXiv: riemann

item.title: On the Cohomological Amplitude of the Locally Analytic Jacquet--Langlands Functor
item.description: We prove a local cohomological bound $RΓ_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}(X,\mathcal F)\in D^{[0,\dim X]}$ for a pro-étale sheaf with a derived $p$-complete integral lattice whose modulo $p^m$ reductions are filtered colimits of finite local systems on an affinoid topologically of finite type over $C$. For $G=\mathrm{GL}_n(F)$, with $n\geq2$ and $F/\mathbb Q_p$ finite, we apply these local bounds to variants of Scholze's Jacquet--Langlands functor $\mathrm{JL}_\mathscr{B}(Π):= RΓ_{\mathrm{pro\acute… — Yu Xiao — arXiv: langlands

item.title: Zeta function in Coulomb background
item.description: We calculate the one-loop vacuum energy of a massive scalar field confined to the interior of a sphere with Dirichlet boundary conditions and subject to a Coulomb background potential $α/r$. The spectrum is determined by the zeros of a confluent hypergeometric (Kummer) function, and the corresponding zeta function is constructed and analytically continued to $s=-1/2$. The renormalization is performed by subtracting the divergent part of the zeta function, defined through the heat kernel expansion, which removes… — M. Bordag, I. G. Pirozhenko — arXiv: riemann

item.title: On mod p Hecke algebras of abstract p-adic automorphic forms
item.description: We study completed local shallow Hecke algebras acting on residual automorphic forms attached to projective augmented modules for $\GL_2(\Q_p)$. For odd primes $p$, we prove that the maximal ideal has nilpotence exponent $O(p^{r/2})$ on the level-$r$ generalized eigenspace. For $p\ge5$, if the corresponding Hecke eigenspace in the residual smooth dual has finite length as a $\GL_2(\Q_p)$-representation, then the completed local algebra is noetherian of Krull dimension at least two. If, in addition, its cotangent… — Nha Xuan Truong — arXiv: modularity

item.title: A quantitative two-interval criterion for the Riemann hypothesis
item.description: We aim to study whether the Weil form can detect a zero of the Riemann zeta function away from the critical line using two functions with increasingly narrow, widely separated supports. We prove that the Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality on every such pair at all sufficiently large separations, provided the component widths decrease subexponentially. A zero to the right of the critical line forces the normalized cross term to exceed an exponential at arbitrarily large separations… — Payam Danesh — arXiv: riemann

item.title: Some instances of modularity for residually reducible representations in the mixed case
item.description: Let $F$ be a totally real field, abelian over $\Q$, in which an odd prime $p$ splits completely, and let $ρ:G_F\to\GL_2(\overline\Q_p)$ be an odd irreducible representation which is de Rham with distinct Hodge--Tate weights at the places above $p$ and whose residual representation is reducible. We consider the \emph{mixed} case of the Fontaine--Mazur conjecture, in which $ρ$ is reducible at some places above $p$ and irreducible at the others. This case is not covered by the work of Pan and Zhang. We prove some… — Luis V. Dieulefait — arXiv: modularity

item.title: Anticyclotomic Iwasawa theory at potentially ordinary primes
item.description: We study anticyclotomic Iwasawa theory for self-dual twists of $p$-ordinary modular forms of weight two with nebentype $ε^2$, where $ε$ is a non-trivial Dirichlet character of conductor $p$. Under a generalized Heegner hypothesis and suitable residual hypotheses, we prove one divisibility in the anticyclotomic main conjecture in both the definite and indefinite settings. The prime $p$ may split, remain inert, or ramify in the imaginary quadratic field. Our proofs use a compatible bipartite Euler system of Heegner… — Antonio Lei, Peter Neamti — arXiv: elliptic / arXiv: modularity / arXiv: riemann

item.title: Almost primes in short intervals and averages of long Dirichlet polynomial approximations to $(ζ'/ζ)^{k}$
item.description: We study the asymptotic behaviour of the mean square of long truncations of the Dirichlet series for $\bigl(ζ'/ζ\bigr)^{k}$ on the critical line; we establish the connection between this problem and the short-interval variance of the convoluted von Mangoldt function $Λ^{*k}$ in short intervals and in arithmetic progressions. Under a shifted moments conjecture and the Riemann Hypothesis (RH), we prove that the short-interval variance leading coefficient is the derivative of the mean-square leading coefficient. A… — Siegfred Baluyot, John Brian Conrey, Ayesha Irfan, Nina C. Snaith — arXiv: riemann

item.title: Geometrization of Kottwitz-Shelstad transfer and Vogan's conjecture on local Arthur packets
item.description: We give a geometric analogue of Kottwitz-Shelstad transfer for a general class of reductive groups over p-adic fields with cyclic component groups of trivial or prime order. We prove that this geometric transfer coincides with Kottwitz-Shelstad transfer, adapted to the language of disconnected groups, assuming the local Langlands correspondence satisfying certain desiderata, including the Kazhdan-Lusztig hypothesis for the ambient group and its endoscopic groups. As an application of this geometrization, we prove… — Clifton Cunningham, Alexander Hazeltine, Baiying Liu, Chi-Heng Lo, Mishty Ray, Bin Xu — arXiv: langlands

item.title: Resurgence and Modularity in the First Painlevé Equation
item.description: For the first Painlevé equation, we relate three nonlinear Stokes maps associated with a full turn around infinity to modular transformations of the two-parameter tau function through the identity $\boldsymbol S_π\circ\boldsymbol S_0\circ \boldsymbol S_{-π}=\mathsf S\circ\mathsf T$. Here the subscripts label Borel directions, while $\mathsf S$ and $\mathsf T$ denote the modular generators. Working under the analytic assumptions of the topological recursion and exact WKB constructions, we compare Stokes… — Kohei Iwaki, Noam Tamarin — arXiv: modularity

item.title: Cell-type-specific modularity in E/I networks shapes dynamical regimes and computational capabilities
item.description: Structural modularity is a ubiquitous feature of brain networks that shapes neural dynamics and information processing. Yet excitatory and inhibitory populations can differ in their modular organization, and it remains unclear how this asymmetry affects network dynamics and computation. Here, using dynamical mean-field theory and simulations of networks performing complex temporal tasks, we show that independently tuning excitatory and inhibitory modularity controls the dynamical regimes of balanced E/I networks… — Emmanouil Giannakakis, Victor Buendía, Oleg Vinogradov, Anna Levina — arXiv: modularity

item.title: The Art of Orbifolding by Huge Non-Abelian Groups
item.description: We compute torus partition functions of orbifolds of two-dimensional chiral fermions by huge non-Abelian groups involving the Conway group, one of the sporadic finite simple groups. This seemingly standard problem turns out to contain, somewhat unexpectedly, multiple major issues hitherto unresolved, both at the level of the principle and at the level of practice. We describe in detail how they can be overcome. Although the methods described in this paper are generally applicable, the choice of the particular… — Jan Albert, Masaki Okada, Yuji Tachikawa — arXiv: modularity

item.title: An information-geometric formulation of distributed computation
item.description: Understanding how complex systems perform computations, i.e. how they store, transmit, and transform information across their components, is a major goal across the natural sciences. However, characterising genuinely collective computations across multiple inputs and outputs that cannot be reduced to contributions from individual components remains an open problem. In this work, we introduce $Φ\text{ID}^{IG}$, a geometric theory of information dynamics that captures irreducible collective phenomena and enables a… — Alberto Liardi, George Blackburne, Pedro A. M. Mediano — arXiv: modularity

item.title: Moments of characteristic polynomials at random matrix Gram points
item.description: We evaluate the characteristic polynomial of a random unitary matrix at the points on the unit circle where the polynomial takes real values. In analogy to the Riemann zeta function we call these the ``random matrix Gram points''. On the random matrix side we answer in the affirmative a question of Richard Hall, who expected that zeta on the Gram points should be larger than typical. We prove that for any fixed positive $k$, the $2k$th moment of the characteristic polynomial averaged over the random matrix Gram… — Christopher Hughes, Somin Kim — arXiv: random matrix / arXiv: riemann

item.title: Stop Handcrafting Your Engine! GenDB-V: Towards AI-Generated and Formally Verified Database Systems
item.description: For over 50 years, the database community has developed a wide range of successful engines to answer two fundamental questions: how can database systems run faster, and how can we ensure their correctness? Experience with these engines shows that performance depends on hardware and workloads. As both change over time, we repeatedly redesign and rebuild database systems, a time-consuming and expensive process. Correctness remains another long-standing challenge: recent studies continue to uncover wrong-answer bugs… — Jiale Lao, Immanuel Trummer — arXiv: modularity

item.title: On the generic case of Jiang's conjecture
item.description: Jiang's conjecture predicts that if $π$ is a generic representation of a quasi-split $p$-adic group, then the $L$-parameter of the Aubert-Zelevinsky involution of $π$ must be trivial on $\mathrm{SL}_2$. In this paper, we prove this statement for a general quasi-split group under certain assumptions on the conjectural local Langlands correspondence. — Chi-Heng Lo — arXiv: langlands

item.title: Topological transcendence degree and the dimension problem for perfectoid spaces
item.description: Let $K$ be a perfectoid field of characteristic $p$ with countable value group (for example, $K=\mathbb{C}_{p}^{\flat}$). We study Zariski-closed subsets \begin{equation*}Z\subseteq \mathbb{B}_{K}^{n,\mathrm{perfd}}\end{equation*}of the $n$-dimensional perfectoid closed unit ball $\mathbb{B}_{K}^{n,\mathrm{perfd}}$ over $K$. We use an example of Gleason, and its generalization obtained in the authors' previous work, to show that two natural notions of dimension for such Zariski-closed subsets, the Krull dimension… — Dimitri Dine, Jack J Garzella — arXiv: perfectoid

item.title: Probing automorphic induction through zero correlations and secondary arithmetic terms
item.description: Zero correlations offer a way to test the cuspidal structure of an automorphic L-function, but their leading self statistics retain only coarse degree and multiplicity data. We therefore adjoin a specified cuspidal L-function as a probe and study the resulting raw mixed correlations. Assuming a factorization into cuspidal L-functions over Q, we show that a mixed pair statistic detects the probe's occurrence and recovers its multiplicity. A suitable Gevrey-order-two test eliminates the smooth-density terms and… — Yangbo Ye — arXiv: riemann

item.title: Convergence in law of the maximum of the Riemann zeta function on expanding intervals near the critical line
item.description: Let $T \to \infty$, let $τ$ be uniformly distributed on $[T,2T]$, and let $σ= σ(T)$ be a deterministic real part approaching $1/2$ from the right. We establish the convergence in law of the recentered maximum of $\log|ζ(σ+ \mathrm{i}τ+ \mathrm{i} h)|$ over $I_θ = \smash{[ - (\log T)^θ,(\log T)^θ]}$, for every fixed $θ> 0$. Under explicit conditions on the displacement $σ- 1/2$, the recentered maximum converges to a Gumbel distribution with scale parameter $1/(2\sqrt{1 + θ})$. The recentering is an exact upper… — Frédéric Ouimet — arXiv: riemann

item.title: Cuspidal sheaves on the stack of L-parameters
item.description: We introduce the notion of cuspidal coherent sheaves on the moduli stack of local L-parameters. We give a complete classification and relate them to Lusztig's cuspidal local systems (or character sheaves). Under the categorical local Langlands conjecture, these sheaves are expected to correspond to supercuspidal representations supported at basic points. We also construct semiorthogonal decompositions of the category of coherent sheaves on the moduli stack of L-parameters that conjecturally match the… — Alexander Bertoloni Meli, Teruhisa Koshikawa — arXiv: langlands

item.title: Grassmannians of absolute Banach-Colmez Spaces
item.description: We introduce Grassmannians of absolute Banach--Colmez spaces and prove the $k$-Grassmannian is perfectoid if and only if the space has slope $< 1/k$. For $d=1$, this proves a conjecture of Hansen--Mann. The key ingredient is a Plücker morphism, which realizes the $k$-Grassmannian of a slope $d/n$ space as a Zariski closed subspace of the projectivization of a slope $kd/n$ space. We also introduce a general method to construct invariant elements in perfectoid Tate--Huber pairs, and use this to prove absolute… — Zecheng Yi — arXiv: langlands / arXiv: perfectoid

item.title: Deterministic Root-Finding over Finite Fields with Elliptic Curves
item.description: Finding the roots of a polynomial over a finite field $\mathbb F_q$ in deterministic polynomial time is a long-standing open problem. Classical deterministic methods work in the multiplicative group $\mathbb F_q^\times$ and are efficient only when $q-1$ is smooth, which is rarely the case. We propose a method that replaces $\mathbb F_q^\times$ by the groups of rational points of an elliptic curve $E$ and of its quadratic twist $\widetilde E$. The computation splits into an offline phase, which depends only on… — Pierre-Jean Spaenlehauer — arXiv: elliptic

item.title: Gross--Prasad conjecture in geometric Langlands
item.description: We prove part of the global Gross--Prasad conjecture for $G = \mathrm{SO}_{n} \times \mathrm{SO}_{n-1}$ and $H = \mathrm{SO}_{n-1}$ in the unramified de Rham geometric Langlands setting proposed by Ben-Zvi--Sakellaridis--Venkatesh. — Kaiyi Chen, Zeyu Wang — arXiv: langlands

item.title: Entanglement for elliptic curve group orders
item.description: For an elliptic curve $E$ defined over a number field $K$ and $\mathfrak{p}$ a prime of good reduction of $E/K$, we let $n_\mathfrak{p}=\#E(k_\mathfrak{p})$ be the order of the group of points over the residue class field $k_\mathfrak{p}$. Divisibility of $n_\mathfrak{p}$ by a prime $\ell$ depends on the splitting behavior of $\mathfrak{p}$ in the $\ell$-division field $K(E[\ell](\bar{K}))$ of $E$ and, generically, divisibility of $n_\mathfrak{p}$ by different primes $\ell_1$ and $\ell_2$ are `independent events'… — Francesco Campagna, Nathan Jones, Francesco Pappalardi, Peter Stevenhagen — arXiv: elliptic

item.title: Stability conditions on Calabi-Yau threefolds of type K
item.description: A Calabi-Yau threefold of type K is a free quotient $X=(S\times E)/G$ of the product of a K3 surface and an elliptic curve. We construct a family of geometric Bridgeland stability conditions on $X$ by using Liu's product construction on $S\times E$ and then inducing along the Galois covering. The family has dimension $2h^{1,1}(X)$, and is disjoint from the $\widetilde{\GL}_2^+(\R)$-orbit of Li's stability conditions. These threefolds carry a K3 fibration, and the pushforward of an object from a smooth K3 fiber is… — Uttaran Dutta — arXiv: elliptic / arXiv: hodge

item.title: Rational points of exact period three for the quadratic family
item.description: For the quadratic family $f_c(x) = x^2 + c$ over $\Q$, we isolate a general $S$-unit and ABC template for rational periodic cycles: under the ABC conjecture, any rational quantity built from the consecutive-point sums of a rational period-$n$ cycle whose value and shift-by-$1$ are both $S$-units (with $S$ the support of the denominator of $c$) has logarithmic height at most $(1+\eps)\sum_{p \in S} \log p + O_\eps(1)$. Specializing to period $3$ in the change of coordinates $u = x_0 + x_1$ and $v = x_0 + x_2$, the… — Antti Käenmäki, Pekka Kosunen — arXiv: elliptic

item.title: Central values of additive twists of automorphic $L$-series
item.description: We study series $L(x,s):=\sum_n ρ(n)e^{2πi n x}/n^s$, where $ρ(n)$ are Fourier coefficients of an automorphic form $φ$ for a discrete cofinite subgroup $Γ\subset \mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ and $x\in\mathbb{R}$. Let $\mathfrak{b}\in\mathbb{R}\cup\{\infty\}$ represent a cusp of $Γ$. Ordering the orbit $Γ\mathfrak{b}$ by increasing denominators, we prove that the values $L(x,1/2)$ for $x\inΓ\mathfrak{b}$, suitably normalized, become equidistributed according to a standard complex Gaussian law, under natural… — Sandro Bettin, Sary Drappeau, Jungwon Lee — arXiv: riemann

item.title: On the modularity of residually reducible Galois representations of rank 2
item.description: We use a new version of the Taylor--Wiles method, based on a tame analogue of the techniques introduced by Skinner--Wiles, to prove new modularity theorems for residually reducible Galois representations of rank 2 over totally real fields. — Andrea Dotto, Jack A. Thorne — arXiv: modularity

item.title: Joint universality of the Riemann zeta-function with arbitrary real shift parameters
item.description: We prove joint universality of the Riemann zeta-function for shifts $ζ(s+id_jτ)$ with arbitrary nonzero real parameters $d_j$ whose absolute values are pairwise distinct, and show that these conditions are optimal. As a consequence, we establish generalized strong recurrence for every finite family of nonzero real parameters, meaning that the corresponding shifts of the Riemann zeta-function simultaneously approximate each other. The only cases for which generalized strong recurrence remains unproved are those… — Łukasz Pańkowski — arXiv: riemann

item.title: CA2 numbers and the Riemann hypothesis: a numerical investigation of Ramanujan's inequalities
item.description: Robin's criterion reduces the Riemann hypothesis to an inequality for colossally abundant (CA) numbers, and Wu's theorem reduces the test further to the subclass CA2. We study this reduction numerically and consider smaller subsets on which the same criterion remains sufficient. We also show that the logarithmic decay law suggested by Briggs's computations follows from Ramanujan's conditional bounds. To investigate the next term, we compare the normalized Robin difference with Ramanujan's oscillatory expression… — Dmitry R. Leshchiner, Oleg R. Musin, James Thompson — arXiv: riemann

item.title: A p-adic Valuation Calculus for Permutations with Restricted Cycle Lengths
item.description: Let a_A(n) be the number of permutations of {1,...,n} all of whose cycle lengths lie in a set A. We develop a valuation calculus for these numbers. Mobius inversion writes the exponential generating function as an Euler product, and at a prime p the factors with non-p-integral exponents, the blocks, determine a finite knapsack problem. Its optimal value gives a lower bound for v_p(a_A(n)), and the bound is attained exactly when one residue modulo p, the sum of the terms of the optimal choices, does not vanish… — Ahaan Kallat — arXiv: lean

item.title: Crossed modularity of twisted VOA modules
item.description: Let $V$ be a strongly rational vertex operator algebra and $G\leq\operatorname{Aut}(V)$ a finite group. Using the $G$-crossed braided fusion structure of twisted modules constructed in \cite{Crossed}, we prove that the conformal twist $e^{2πiL(0)}$ gives a crossed ribbon structure and that the crossed category is modular in Kirillov's sense. Consequently, its equivariantization is a modular tensor category. We also obtain dimension and simple-object counting formulas for the twisted sectors. — Shun Xu — arXiv: modularity / arXiv: tqft

item.title: On Hecke algebras at exceptional Eisenstein primes
item.description: We study the structure over $\mathbb{Z}_p$ of the Hecke algebra acting on ordinary cusp forms in the Eisenstein, non-$p$-distinguished case. Our results and methods draw on four complementary approaches: deformation theory, through $R=\mathbf{T}$ theorems; Iwasawa theory, through connections to Sharifi's conjecture; $p$-adic $L$-functions, through an exceptional zero formula; and computational experiments using Magma. We also obtain new results regarding the Coleman--Greenberg conjecture. — Alexandre Maksoud — arXiv: riemann

item.title: Motivic local density of isolated singularities of algebraic varieties
item.description: The goal of this paper is to compute the motivic local density of an isolated singularity of an algebraic variety, in order to explain its link with algebraic multiplicity. We compute the density as the residue in 1 of a Zeta function associated to normalized local volumes and we use a resolution of the singularity to get the formula. — Sidonie Ratajczak — arXiv: riemann

item.title: Spectral $L^2$-bounds on Eisenstein series and Diophantine properties of quadratic forms
item.description: We give $L^2$-bounds with respect to the height of the spectral parameter for Epstein zeta functions $\mathrm{Z}_Q(s)$ and non-holomorphic Eisenstein series $E_{\mathfrak{c}}(s,z)$ attached to the Hecke congruence subgroup $Γ_0 (p)$ of prime level $p$. Our bounds are completely explicit in the level and, additionally, constitute an almost sure logarithmic improvement over previously established bounds for the level-one Eisenstein series. Following the approach of Kelmer--Kontorovich--Lutsko, we combine the… — Jitendra Bajpai, Kristian Holm — arXiv: riemann

item.title: CaLLM: Continual Adaptation of LLMs via Non-Parametric Adapter Routing
item.description: Continual adaptation of large language models (LLMs) to evolving task distributions while mitigating catastrophic forgetting remains an open problem. Existing strategies often struggle to scale or lack a robust mechanism for zero-shot task-to-expert assignment. We introduce CaLLM, a framework that resolves these tensions by combining metric-based meta-learning with modular parameter isolation via lightweight adapters. First, CaLLM projects each input batch into a task-agnostic embedding space to find its nearest… — Bilge Celik, Anna Vettoruzzo, Joaquin Vanschoren — arXiv: modularity

item.title: Elliptic curve rank growth in multi-quadratic extensions
item.description: In this article we give an algorithm to produce infinitely many explicit quadratic twists of a given elliptic curve over $\mathbb{Q}$ with a rational point and fixed root number. Moreover, under the Parity Conjecture (or other technical hypotheses), for each $n\geq 1$, we produce explicit multi-quadratic extensions $L_n$ of $\mathbb{Q}$, of degree $2^n$, such that the growth in rank from $\mathbb{Q}$ to $L_n$ is at least $\max\{2n+2^{n-1}-1,\,2^n-1\}$ when the root number of $E$ is $-1$, and at least… — Dylan T. Costa, Álvaro Lozano-Robledo — arXiv: elliptic

item.title: Jack multiple zeta function
item.description: For conjugate shapes $λ$ and $λ'$, Stanley's duality relates the Jack symmetric functions $J_λ(x;α)$ and $J_{λ'}(x;1/α)$. Through Stanley's combinatorial formula, it is an identity between the sums of the weights of the semi-standard Young tableaux giving the same monomial. We introduce the Jack multiple zeta functions, which keep these weights separate, and prove that Stanley's duality lifts to them, including the case of skew shapes. Thus the duality holds before the weights are summed up, and in fact step by… — Maki Nakasuji, Wataru Takeda — arXiv: riemann

item.title: How to get an attractive model
item.description: We give a fourth-order Calabi-Yau differential operator, which seems to have been missed by earlier tabulations. We draw attention to this operator because of its clear geometric interpretation and evidence that it possesses a rank-two attractor, conjecturally giving a new example of a Calabi-Yau threefold with modularity properties analogous to those of an elliptic curve over $\mathbb{Q}$. — Joseph McGovern — arXiv: elliptic / arXiv: hodge / arXiv: modularity

item.title: Heavy Heisenberg Algebras, Zero Modes and Modularity
item.description: It is known due to a result of Miyamoto that zero mode correlators of weight $1$ vectors of vertex operator algebras are quasi-modular forms, and that their generating series are Jacobi forms. In this article we generalize this to higher weight vectors. We consider weight 2 vectors that generate what we call heavy Heisenberg algebras. We prove that their zero mode correlators are a specific type of quasi-modular forms. As a consequence, they too can be summed up into a generating series with Jacobi-like modular… — Darlayne Addabbo, Christoph A. Keller — arXiv: modularity / arXiv: tqft

item.title: Frangible prime gaps
item.description: A prime gap $(p_n, p_{n+1})$ is \textit{frangible} if the smallest prime divisor of every integer $m$ with $p_n — Michael J. Mossinghoff, Timothy S. Trudgian — arXiv: primes

item.title: Stability of certain elements in the Bernstein center
item.description: Let $G$ be a split connected reductive algebraic group over a non-archimedean local field $F$ of characteristic zero. The stable center conjecture asserts that the subspace of stable elements in the Bernstein center of $G(F)$ is a sub-algebra, and this subring is conjecturally isomorphic to the regular functions on the moduli of semi-simple Langlands parameters. Bezrukavnikov-Kazhdan-Varshavsky suggested an approach towards the stable center conjecture by explicitly constructing elements and proving their… — Sarbartha Bhattacharya, Shenghao Li — arXiv: langlands

item.title: Supercuspidal blocks and the local Langlands correspondence
item.description: Let $G$ be a connected reductive group defined over a non-archimedean local field $F$, and let $\mathrm{Rep}^{\mathfrak{s}}(G(F))$ be a supercuspidal Bernstein block. In this paper, we define a cohomology class $[μ_{\mathfrak{s}}]$ represented by a 2-cocycle that encodes the equivalence class of $\mathrm{Rep}^{\mathfrak{s}}(G(F))$. We then formulate a conjecture describing $[μ_{\mathfrak{s}}]$ in terms of the enhanced $L$-parameter $(\varphi, ρ)$ attached to an irreducible representation in… — Noriyuki Abe, Kazuma Ohara — arXiv: langlands

item.title: Quantum-Seeded Distributed Post-Quantum Group Signatures for 5G V2X Communications
item.description: Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) communications rely on elliptic-curve signatures that a quantum adversary breaks and on pseudonym certificates whose anonymity rests on rotation rate, not cryptography. This work presents qDGSP, a post-quantum V2X infrastructure: a hash-based dynamic group signature scheme (DGSP, over SPHINCS+ and WOTS+) distributed between a central controller and roadside verifiers. Group keys derive deterministically from quantum key distribution (QKD) seeds served over the ETSI GS QKD 014… — P. Blanco-Casal, P. Rejo-Iglesias, D. Cajaraville-Aboy, J. Vecino-Peñas, R. P. Díaz-Redondo, A. Fernández-Vilas — arXiv: elliptic

item.title: Noetherian local rings without perfectoid towers
item.description: Let $k$ be a perfect field of characteristic $p>0$. We prove that if a $p$-torsionfree ring $R$, defined by homogeneous equations over $W(k)$, admits a perfectoid tower arising from $(R,(p))$, then its special fiber is $F$-liftable. We also give explicit examples admitting no such tower, including examples with $F$-liftable special fibers. — Tatsuki Yamaguchi — arXiv: perfectoid

item.title: Langlands-Shahidi gamma factors and local transfer in families
item.description: Let $G$ be a quasi-split $p$-adic group, defined over a non-archimedean local field of residue cardinality $q$, and $R$ be a $\mathbb{Z}[\sqrt{q}^{-1},μ_{4p^\infty}]$-algebra. We generalize the constructions of Shahidi local coefficients and Langlands-Shahidi gamma factors to the setting of co-Whittaker $R$-representations. For classical $p$-adic groups, we prove there is a unique integral morphism of endomorphism rings of Gelfand--Graev representations, interpolating the (standard) local generic transfer to a… — Johannes Girsch, Robert Kurinczuk — arXiv: langlands

item.title: Schäffer's conjecture for even $k \le 42$
item.description: In 1956, Schäffer made a conjecture on the whole number solutions to the Diophantine equation $S_k(x):=1^k+2^k+\cdots+x^k=y^n$. In this paper we show how for even $k$, we can descend to a long list of three coupled equations of the form $Ax^p-By^p=1$, where $A,B\in\mathbb{Q}$. To this system, we apply the modular method, linear forms in logarithms, and local methods. As a result, we prove Schäffer's conjecture for even $k \le 42$. — Imin Chen, Stephen Choi, James Houle — arXiv: modularity

item.title: CFBrainAug: Modularity-Induced Counterfactual Brain Network Augmentation for Interpretable fMRI-based Autism Diagnosis
item.description: Machine learning on resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI) brain networks is promising for diagnosing Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD), but existing methods are prone to overfitting on limited training data, and their post-hoc statistical attribution offers limited clinical interpretability. We propose CFBrainAug, a counterfactual brain network learning framework that unifies data augmentation and counterfactual explanation by learning label-altered brain networks. Unlike conventional… — Yifan Qiao, Sheng Li — arXiv: modularity
